speaker: john_heminges
text: He is in the yard. Leave him there. The ink is the work now, and the book is the other work, and neither of them needs a boy leaning on a wet word.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: A quarter of an hour under the weight. I said so. My sleeve has the scars of men who thought a word was dry because they were tired of waiting.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not tired of the decision. I am tired of standing over it. Put the eightpence where copying goes, and let the rolls alone until a cuff will not lift them.

speaker: john_heminges
text: I am putting it. One line. I will not strike a total under a morning that is not finished, and I will not write gift in a book I have to read aloud on Saturday.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Gift would be a lie, and a lie in that book outlives the man who thought he was being kind. Copying is the word. It is a small word. It will fit.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Copying. Eightpence. Out of the stock. If anyone in the yard asks what we did, they may be told we made three rolls agree. They may not be told the shape of the sign.

speaker: john_heminges
text: They will not hear it from me. Fetch the book to the chest, not to the trestle. I will not have wet ink and wet money on the same board.
